name: Bento
tagline: A full PowerPoint alternative living in a single HTML file — deck, fonts, images, charts, animations, and editor all in one
description: Bento is a presentation tool that ships as one self-contained HTML file: open it in any browser to edit, present, and send an entire deck without installing anything. The whole thing — slides, fonts, images, charts, animations, and the editor itself — is packaged into a single ~560KB shell, so a finished presentation is just a file you can email or host. Under the hood the document is honest plaintext JSON, which means AI agents can edit a deck in place by rewriting the JSON, and the editor is built on its own CRDT for real-time collaboration. Real-time editing is end-to-end encrypted with AES-GCM, and morph transitions give presenting a native slide-software feel. TypeScript and MIT-licensed, with 3.9k stars.
highlights: Entire app — deck, fonts, images, charts, animations, and editor — in one ~560KB HTML file
View-source-honest: the document is plaintext JSON, so AI agents can edit decks in place
End-to-end encrypted collaboration (AES-GCM) over its own CRDT
Morph-style transitions and built-in charts amount to a credible PowerPoint alternative
Open in any browser, edit, present, and send — no install, no account
curatorNote: The single-file + plaintext-JSON combination is the clever bit: a slide deck that is literally editable by an LLM, while still being a real product you can present from. Watching the AI-ready angle mature is the reason to keep an eye on it.
